clue.text: Tie-pin came undone through restlessness

indicators.note: something that came undone has fallen apart, so the letters of the words before it are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A tie-pin keeps slipping loose, and the wearer fidgets impatiently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came undone' rearranges TIEPINCAME, the letters of 'Tie-pin' plus 'came' itself; the fodder here is the whole run before the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to wait calmly shows itself as fidgety unease, a near synonym.

clue.text: Very small character

parts.note: reads like a description of a tiny person but means the slightest letter of the Greek alphabet, whose name also stands for a tiny amount

explanation.definitionFit: The ninth Greek letter is the smallest in form, and its name is an idiom for the least possible quantity.

clue.text: Flare up after father makes a fuss

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Flare up after father makes a fuss (7)' as held gives PA + an anagram of FLARE, but the held answer PARAFLE is not a word, and no real word of seven letters fits; answer or clue misread.
annotationWithheld.clue: Flare up after father makes a fuss

clue.text: One old fort now turned into a tourist attraction

indicators.note: turned here means converted or twisted around, telling us to rearrange the letters of the old fort phrase

parts.note: taken as written, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: An ancient fortress has been converted into a sightseeing destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges ONEOLDFORTNOW; 'into' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic Thames-side castle housing the Crown Jewels is one of the most visited sights in the British capital.

clue.text: Flea-bane is about to be found in troubled region

indicators.note: to be found in says the short word for about goes in among the letters of region, joining the pool that gets mixed
troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters of region are mixed

parts.note: re is Latin for 'about', as in a memo's subject line
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remedy for fleas turns up in a disturbed part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be found in' puts the two letters for 'about' among those of 'region', and 'troubled' rearranges all eight together; 'is' is a link word. Fleabane is a daisy-like plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleabane genus of daisy-like plants, once thought to drive away insects, has this botanical name.

clue.text: First cook gets second wind

indicators.note: the cook gets, or takes in, an extra letter, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a chef is a professional cook

indicators.note: second here points at the second letter of the word wind

explanation.surface: A head cook catches his breath again after a hard service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' takes I, the second letter of 'wind', and 'gets' puts it inside CHEF. 'Second wind' reads as a fresh burst of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal or foremost in rank, as in a chief executive.

clue.text: Ran away from some wasp Edward caught

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of their letters is taken, giving a run tucked inside them

explanation.surface: Someone fled from a wasp that Edward had trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from some' points inside 'wasp Edward', where the letters run waSP EDward; 'caught' adds to the picture and supports the reading of letters held within.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry off quickly, past tense of the verb meaning to go fast.

clue.text: This could be introduced to add flavour to.10

definitions.text: This could be introduced to add flavour to.10

parts.words: This could be introduced to add flavour to.10
parts.note: describes an ingredient for flavouring the mutton dish at 10 across: a leafy green grown for the cooking pot

explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is IRISH STEW, a mutton stew; the clue refers to a herb put in the pot for flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A culinary herb or vegetable grown for seasoning stews and soups is called by this name.

clue.text: Flight after feathers fall to a lower position

indicators.note: after places the flight second, following the feathers

parts.note: down is the soft fine feathers of a bird
a flight is a set of steps between floors

explanation.surface: After a bird's plumage falls, it drifts lower and lower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' is a link word. 'feathers' and 'Flight' look like birds in the surface, but one is soft plumage and the other a run of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving to the floor beneath, as in going down to the ground floor of a house.

clue.text: Might be worth a toss

parts.note: sounds like saying something is barely valuable, but describes the single cast of a ball or dart, as in a price per go

explanation.definitionFit: A toss is a single hurl or cast, and the phrase 'a go' is priced per such cast at a fairground stall.

clue.text: Mutton dish which rises with cooking

indicators.note: cooking means something is being prepared or fiddled with, telling us to rearrange letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lamb casserole swells up in the pot as it simmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges RISESWITH; 'which' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional stew of mutton, potatoes and onions from Ireland.

clue.text: Awaiting the arrival of the bypass perhaps, without much enthusiasm

definitions.text: Awaiting the arrival of the bypass perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: A patient waiting for heart bypass surgery has a heart only half working; the everyday sense is with little keenness or commitment.

clue.text: Fergusson left disorder as a result of a poor memory

indicators.note: disorder means a jumbled state, so the letters of the name and the word after it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Fergusson walked away from a mess because he could not remember things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' rearranges FERGUSSONLEFT; 'as a result of' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of failing to recall things, a tendency to absent-mindedness.

clue.text: Expression of great delight from smug fellow

explanation.definitionFit: A childish exclamation of glee; also a self-righteous person who parades their own virtue.

clue.text: Flood is finished, afterwards run smoothly

indicators.note: afterwards places the smooth running second, following the finished part

parts.note: when something is finished it is over
liquids flow when they run smoothly

explanation.surface: The deluge has ended, and afterwards the waters run gently again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flood' looks like a noun beside 'finished', but it is a verb, meaning to spill over.
explanation.definitionFit: To spill over the banks or brim, as water does in a deluge.

clue.text: Irrational fear that father might come round when first hearing of boy's indiscretion

indicators.note: the father comes round, or surrounds, the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A dread that Dad will visit as soon as he hears of his son's misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word; 'might' belongs to the surface. The initials come from four words in a row: hearing, of, boy's, indiscretion.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong, unreasoning dread of something specific, such as spiders or heights.

clue.text: Continental good about correct choice of seaside resort

indicators.note: about here means around, so the French word wraps the other piece

parts.note: bon is French for good, continental meaning from mainland Europe
right means correct

explanation.surface: A European says it is fine to pick a particular beach town for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choice of' is a link phrase. 'Continental' tells us the word for good is French. The resort is on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A large holiday town on the Sussex coast of southern England, famous for its pier.

clue.text: House officer saw first casualty trolley in the entrance!

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the two initials go within the entrance

parts.note: a door is the way in to a building

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: At a hospital, a junior medic spotted the first patient lying on a trolley in the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is a link word. A house officer is a junior hospital medic in Britain, so 'House' is not a home.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a newly qualified medic in the first job is called a house officer.

clue.text: Firm having a last fling at 16 maybe

parts.note: co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: a fling throws something about, so the letters of the phrase after it are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A company enjoys one final spree at the seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word. 16 down is BRIGHTON, a seaside town, so the definition points to a place beside the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort on the sea, like the one at 16 down, lies beside the shore, so it is by the sea.

clue.text: Settler called soldiers from two regiments back round

indicators.note: round means the reversed regiments go around the word for called
back turns each of the two regiment abbreviations backwards in place

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery and RE the Royal Engineers, two British army regiments
RE is the Royal Engineers, the second regiment
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: A colonist phoned some troops, who came back round again.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Artillery and Royal Engineers are the two regiments; 'back' turns each abbreviation in place before 'round' wraps them about the word for called.
explanation.definitionFit: One who settles or sorts matters out, as in settling a dispute or plans, is an organiser.

clue.text: Trench in part of India where an ape is found

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the trench sits within the Indian state

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a rill is a small channel or trench cut by running water

explanation.surface: A ditch in an Indian region is the habitat of a primate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' and 'is found' are link words. A rill is a narrow channel, which the clue calls a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the great primates, native to central African forests.

clue.text: Second generation production with lovely child

parts.note: grand means splendid or lovely
a daughter is a female child

explanation.surface: Grandparents admire the beautiful offspring of their own children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A son's or daughter's girl is offspring two generations down.

clue.text: Roam about and start up a love affair …

indicators.note: about means moving around, so the letters are shuffled
start points at the opening letter of the word up

explanation.surface: Wander around and begin a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes U from 'up', and 'about' rearranges ROAM with U.
explanation.definitionFit: French for love, used in English for a secret romance.

clue.text: … object of love might be lido!

indicators.note: might be suggests the word could become something else, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The beloved thing could be a public outdoor swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges LIDO. A lido is a public open-air pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adored or worshipped, a hero or false god.

clue.text: Thoroughly unconscious so not worth considering

parts.note: a knocked-out boxer is out
so and and both join a following clause, as in 'and so'
an idea that is out is rejected

explanation.surface: Someone fully knocked out, and so dismissed from consideration.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete or utter, as in a total scoundrel.

clue.text: Gave out as party started!

parts.note: a do is a party
led means began or opened, as in led off the dancing

explanation.surface: Gifts were distributed as the celebration began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Distributed in small portions, as charity or benefits are handed out.

clue.text: Lock used on US campus?

explanation.definitionFit: A brand of cylinder door lock; also the Ivy League university in Connecticut.

clue.text: Sweet drink at dance

parts.note: brandy is a spirit drink
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Having a drink at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled confection flavoured with a liquor, a kind of old-fashioned candy.
